title: Exploring Distributed Vector Databases Performance on HPC Platforms: A Study with Qdrant
problem: Vector databases enable similarity search critical for RAG-augmented LLMs, but their performance characteristics on HPC systems are unknown; little data on how they scale across multiple nodes
motivation: Vector databases are becoming central to modern AI workflows (LLM grounding, recommendation systems), yet their deployment and performance on high-performance computing systems remains unexplored. Understanding performance characteristics is essential for production deployments.
method: The researchers tested Qdrant, a distributed vector database (a system for finding similar data across multiple computers), by running it on the Polaris supercomputer at Argonne National Laboratory. They used real biological text from the BV-BRC project, converting it to numerical embeddings (mathematical representations capturing text meaning) using the Qwen3-Embedding-4B model. They measured insertion speed, index construction time (building the lookup structure), and query latency (response time for similarity searches), scaling from 1 to 32 worker processes.
key_novelty: This is the first performance study of vector databases (software for finding similar numerical data across multiple computers) on supercomputers, using realistic biological text and extracting practical deployment lessons.
contributions: First empirical study of distributed vector database on HPC supercomputer
Realistic biological text workload and embedding characterization
Query latency characterization with distributed workers
Practical deployment lessons for future research

metrics.primary: Query latency, insertion throughput, index construction time
metrics.workload_size: peS2o corpus embeddings (size not specified in abstract)

limitations: Abstract lacks specific performance numbers; workload size not provided; only Qdrant evaluated (no comparison with Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone); HPC-specific optimizations not discussed
primary_theme: Vector Database Performance on HPC Systems
